faqHeading: Piano Movers FAQ for Boston Customers

faq.q: Do piano movers in Boston move grand pianos?
faq.a: Yes. We move upright and grand pianos, including baby grands, with the extra handling a grand's shape needs.

faq.q: Can you move a piano up or down stairs?
faq.a: Yes. The crew plans the carry on stairs and landings before lifting. Tell us how many steps and turns there are when you request a quote.

faq.q: How is a piano move priced?
faq.a: A local piano move is billed hourly, with travel time from our yard added, and a 2-hour minimum that includes travel time. A move out of state is quoted at a flat rate.

faq.q: Can I move just the piano?
faq.a: Yes. Piano-only moves are common, across town or between rooms of the same home.

faq.q: Will the piano need tuning after the move?
faq.a: Pianos often drift out of tune after a move and a change of room. Book a piano tuner once it has settled in its new spot.

faq.q: What should I measure before a piano move?
faq.a: Measure the doorways, hallway turns and stairwell width on both ends, and note any tight landing. Send those with your quote request so the crew can plan the route and send enough movers.

faqClosing: Still have a question about moving your piano? Our FAQ page covers billing, booking and moving day.

closing.h2: Start Your Piano Move in Boston
closing.body: Tell us the piano type, the stairs and both addresses. The crew plans the carry before moving day, and the floors and walls along the route get covered before the piano moves.
